hero.lead: A nation of 1.41 billion that raised 1.3 trillion yuan through ultra-long special treasury bonds in 2026 alone, and still borrows from the World Bank for clean heating, clean rivers and low-carbon cities.

register.name: RMB green sovereign bonds issued in Canada
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · announced 10 November 2026 · 3-year CNY 2bn at 1.40% · 5-year CNY 2bn at 1.50% · bids of CNY 54.04bn, 13.5 times the amount offered
register.note: The Ministry of Finance’s first sovereign bond issuance in the Canadian market
register.text: Yuan-denominated green sovereign bonds of the People’s Republic of China, issued in Canada in two tranches of three and five years. They follow the Ministry’s green sovereign issue in Hong Kong of May 2026.

register.name: RMB sovereign bonds issued in Hong Kong: further issue of October 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance, through the HKMA Central Moneymarkets Unit · tender 23 October 2026 · issued 27 October 2026 · 1.38% due 2028, CNY 4bn · 1.40% due 2029, CNY 5bn · 1.57% due 2031, CNY 4bn · 1.87% due 2036, CNY 2.5bn
register.note: Amounts offered at the tender; the four bonds were first issued on 13 February 2026
register.text: A further issue, by tender in Hong Kong, of four yuan-denominated treasury bonds maturing between 2028 and 2036. It is part of the Ministry of Finance’s regular issuance of RMB treasury bonds in Hong Kong, which finances the central budget behind the public services of the seven standards.

register.name: Ultra-long special treasury bonds, 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · in the 2026 budget approved on 12 March 2026 · issuance began in April 2026 · CNY 572bn issued in the first half, 44% of the year’s task
register.note: CNY 250bn set aside for consumer goods trade-ins and CNY 105.049bn for high-standard farmland in 2026
register.text: Long-dated central government bonds for major national strategies and security capacity in key areas, large-scale equipment upgrades and consumer goods trade-ins. In the first half of 2026 the Ministry of Finance allocated CNY 606.46 billion of them to 936 major projects, and CNY 105.049 billion, with other funds, to build or upgrade 61.08 million mu of high-standard farmland, which serves the food standard.

register.name: Euro sovereign bonds issued in Luxembourg
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued in Luxembourg, June 2026
register.note: The largest euro bond issue in Asia-Pacific history, at the lowest issue spread, as the Ministry of Finance reports
register.text: Euro-denominated sovereign bonds of the People’s Republic of China, issued in Luxembourg. They finance the central budget, which pays for the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: RMB treasury bonds issued in Hong Kong, first half of 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · regular issuance in Hong Kong · January to June 2026
register.note: Issued on a regular schedule through the year
register.text: Yuan-denominated treasury bonds that the Ministry of Finance issues in Hong Kong on a regular schedule. They finance the central budget, which pays for the public services behind the seven standards.

register.name: RMB green sovereign bonds issued in Hong Kong
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · issued 28 May 2026 · 3-year CNY 3bn at 1.42% · 5-year CNY 3bn at 1.56% · subscriptions CNY 62.4bn, 10.4 times the issue size
register.note: All proceeds go to eligible green expenditures under the central budget
register.text: Yuan-denominated green sovereign bonds of the People’s Republic of China, issued in Hong Kong in three- and five-year tranches. The proceeds are applied to eligible green expenditures under the central budget, following the People’s Republic of China Sovereign Green Bond Framework.

register.name: Special treasury bonds for bank capital, 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · in the 2026 budget approved on 12 March 2026 · for the core tier-one capital of the large state-owned commercial banks
register.note: The Ministry’s report of 9 October 2026 speaks of special treasury bonds to add capital to eight central financial enterprises
register.text: Special treasury bonds to replenish the capital of the large state-owned commercial banks, after CNY 500 billion issued for the same purpose in 2025. The Ministry of Finance states that the added capital strengthens their capacity to operate soundly, withstand risk and serve the real economy.

register.name: Local government special-purpose bonds, 2026 quota
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · new quota in the 2026 budget approved on 12 March 2026 · CNY 2.07tn issued in the first half
register.note: More than 17,000 projects supported in the first half, with over CNY 170bn used as project capital
register.text: The new borrowing quota for local governments, for major projects, the replacement of hidden debt and the clearing of government payment arrears. In the first half of 2026 local governments issued CNY 2.07 trillion of new special bonds, supporting more than 17,000 construction projects.

register.text: An IBRD Program-for-Results loan, which disburses against agreed results, for the integrated management of coastal ecosystems in Hainan province.

register.text: An IBRD loan for the restoration of ecosystems and the conservation of biodiversity in China, approved in June 2025.

register.name: Nature Finance Accelerator Program: Bank of Huzhou
register.detail: AIIB · nonsovereign · approved 28 August 2026
register.note: The second bank in the programme, after the Bank of Jiangsu
register.text: An AIIB loan to the Bank of Huzhou to catalyse private capital for nature finance in support of China’s ecological transition, linked to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.

register.name: Nature Finance Accelerator Program: Bank of Jiangsu
register.detail: AIIB · nonsovereign, senior unsecured loan · concept review 28 May 2026 · approved 24 June 2026
register.note: AIIB plans to work with other partner banks through its on-lending facilities
register.text: An AIIB loan to the Bank of Jiangsu to catalyse private capital for nature finance in support of China’s ecological transition, linked to the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework and to cross-border green finance.

register.name: Health care and elderly care finance: Bank of Tianjin
register.detail: ADB · loan agreement signed 21 May 2026 · in yuan equivalent
register.note: ADB’s first private sector loan to a commercial bank for health care and elderly care finance
register.text: An ADB loan to the Bank of Tianjin, a city commercial bank, to finance health care and elderly care providers: facilities, equipment, IT systems and working capital. It serves the health standard; it is also the bank’s first long-term borrowing from an international financial institution.

register.name: Out-of-hospital pharmaceutical distribution: Yaodou
register.detail: ADB · senior secured loan signed 27 January 2026 · equivalent to $20 million
register.note: Most of Yaodou’s products go to inland provinces, including central and southern regions
register.text: An ADB loan to Zhejiang Xinghan Bona Pharmaceutical Technology (Yaodou) for working capital to expand the distribution of medicines to pharmacies and community health centres. It serves the health standard.

items.name: Xi Han Er car washes
items.text: Car washes that train and employ people with intellectual and developmental disabilities, begun in Shenzhen in 2015 and backed by the China Disabled Persons’ Federation for nationwide expansion. By the end of 2025, 63 Xi Han Er car washes had opened across China, giving stable jobs to nearly 700 workers.

items.name: Inclusion Factory
items.text: A factory in Taicang, Jiangsu, founded in 2014, where workers with intellectual and mental disabilities, including Down syndrome and autism, assemble automotive parts for wages. It began with 12 workers and now employs more than 40, and its consultancy helps a further 30-plus into jobs at mainstream companies (2025).

items.name: Starstart
items.text: A bakery-and-coffee chain in Wenzhou, Zhejiang, built as a supportive workplace for autistic young people. It has eight outlets, with two more planned, and employs 18 autistic young people (2026).
